ai.description: The Crowned River Turtle reaches 50 cm. It is dark brown with a yellow-bordered black crown mark on the head and a yellow stripe behind each eye. The plastron is yellow with dark blotches.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hardella thurjii* is best identified by the distinctive bright yellow or orange longitudinal stripes on the sides of its dark head, which contrast sharply with its skin.
ai.habitat: The Crowned River Turtle inhabits deep, slow-moving rivers and oxbow lakes in the Ganges and Brahmaputra basins, typically preferring areas with dense aquatic vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Crowned River Turtle is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on logs or rocks along riverbanks to regulate its body temperature before foraging for aquatic vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hardella thurjii* is oviparous, laying a single clutch of 8–14 eggs annually. Breeding occurs during the winter months, typically from December to March in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hardella thurjii* is found in the Indo-Gangetic and Brahmaputra river systems, primarily across northern and northeastern India, from lowlands up to 300 meters elevation.
